description.narrative: The project will consist of two sovereign loans from EBRD of up to EUR 150 million and EIB of up to EUR 150 million as well to the Government of Moldova, structured in three tranches, a NIF funding of up to EUR 15.0 million, and technical assistance for implementation of road maintenance reform to be financed out of EBRD Special Shareholders Fund. The operation will enable Moldova to undertake necessary rehabilitation of its national road network.

comment.narrative: The Annual Progress Report of the intervention covering period up to 31 December 2021 on page 4 indicates that for the 6.5 km Bahmut bypass on R1 ChisinauUngheniSculeniRomanian border the construction works are ongoing with physical progress being 45.26 as of the reporting period. The Report states that during Q3 of 2021 The Contractor provided suitable material to fill in embankment and access roads adjustments including haulage and compaction executed profiling and compaction and placed the last layer of embankment drainage layer of ballast h200 mm base course of mineral aggregates stabilized with cement shaping of the subgrade layer formation level and excavation of ditches outside the road cross section. Furthermore During 2022 the Contractor will be focusing on the remaining earthworks pavement and road marking. Thus the actual pavement or laying of asphalt is yet to be carried out.While for the 7.9 km Vulcanesti bypass on the M3 ChisinauGiurgiulesti Romanian border road the Annual Progress Report on page 2 indicates that the tender procedure was cancelled due to expiry of financing conditions on 21 December 2017 and the grant is no longer available to fund the works and supervision.
